newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-OLYMPIC CHAMPION LIU CRASHES.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-OLYMPIC CHAMPION LIU CRASHES.

text.p: Yugoslav Alexander Karakesevic, a modest 109th in the world rankings, outlasted China's Olympic champion Liu Guoliang in a five-game thriller on Friday to reach the men's singles third round at the world table tennis championships.
Liu, seeded joint third and regarded as a strong candidate to dethrone compatriot Kong Liungui, lost 17-21 21-16 21-10 18-21 21-13 in the biggest upset of the tournament.
As soon as Karakesevic won the last point, he was hugged by his excited father, team coach Milivoy who played for Yugoslavia in the 1980s.

Karakasevic senior had a distinctive penholder style unlike his left-handed son's western shakehand grip. Practice with his father was perfect prepararation for facing the penholder Liu and Karakesevic targeted his opponent's backhand to good effect.

Liu, losing finalist at the last world championships when the Chinese swept all seven titles, was never allowed to settle into a rhythm. Karakasevic was able to take the sting out of Liu's heavy top-spin attack and the world No.3 began to snatch at his shots.
The Yugoslav gained a commanding 9-1 lead in the deciding fifth game and duly took his surprise place in the last 32.
Germany's Joerge Rosskopf, one of eight players seeded joint ninth, was another Atlanta Olympic medallist to fall in the second round.
Rosskopf, who took bronze at the Games, was beaten 7-21 21-16 11-21 23-21 21-16 by Sweden's Thomas von Scheele.
The German was in Liu's quarter of the draw which opens the way for Karakesevic.

Two other ninth seeds came to grief. Andrzej Grubba, 40 in two weeks, is past his peak and his first round exit was no great shock, but the same cannot be said for Sweden's 1991 world champion Jorgen Persson.

The Swede was beaten 21-19 21-15 20-22 12-21 21-14 by Chinese teenager Wang Liqin in the second round. Although the 18-year-old Wang is a virtual unknown outside China, he has scored several victories over world champion Kong in domestic competition.
Kong himself had somewhat of a bumpy ride in his second-round match against the Czech Republic's Richard Vyborny, trailing 18-20 in the third set before edging home 22-20 21-16 25-23.

Swedish world No.2 Jan-Ove Waldner, 1989 title-holder and twice a a losing finalist, reached the last 32 without being extended. The European champion won both his matches in straight sets, including an impressive 21-17 21-11 21-17 second round victory over Evgue Chtchetinine of Belarus.
Even more impressive was Vladimir Samsonov of Belarus, the joint No.3, seed, who destroyed Japanese national champion Kiyonobu Iwasaki 21-6 21-6 21-9.

The Chinese were also involved in a major second round upset in the women's event where joint No.3 seed Yang Ying fell 21-17 11-21 17-21 21-11 21-18 against Anne Boileau, the big-looping French player who is 88th in the world rankings.
But China's defending champion and Olympic gold medallist Deng Yaping made the last 32 without any problems.
